bpLabel: Fieldstrip Best Practices — this guide follows the Remington 700 bolt-action procedure as documented in Remington’s own Model 700 manual, which Ashbury Precision Ordnance’s own page says the Ashbury Precision Ordnance SABER-M700 shares. It is not Ashbury Precision Ordnance’s manual for this model. If you obtain the factory manual, follow it over this guide. Never take this firearm further apart than this guide goes.
cleanIntro:
No manual from Ashbury Precision Ordnance exists for this model, but Ashbury Precision Ordnance’s own page says the Ashbury Precision Ordnance SABER-M700 carries a Remington 700-pattern action, and that pattern’s owner procedure is documented by Remington’s own Model 700 book. This guide follows it: clear, bolt out at the release the pattern puts inside the trigger guard, the bore from the chamber end, and the bolt back in. If your rifle’s bolt release is not where this guide says, stop — never pull a trigger to find out.

Listed in Fieldstrip as several chamberings. The chambering marked on the gun itself is the one that counts — not this guide, and not the listing.

steps.title: Ammunition out of the room, muzzle somewhere safe
steps.action: Before you start, put every loose cartridge, loaded magazine and box of ammunition in another room — a cleaning bench with live rounds on it is where unintended discharges happen. Keep the muzzle pointed where a shot would hurt no one, and keep your finger outside the trigger guard the whole time. Wear eye protection whenever you use solvent or work near a spring, and work where the air moves.
steps.prose: A safety, if yours has one, is never a substitute for an empty chamber, and nothing in this guide relies on one.

steps.title: Safety fully rearward to S before anything else moves
steps.action: Pull the safety fully rearward to its S position. It is never a substitute for an empty chamber — it is just the first thing the pattern’s own book does, and so does this guide.
steps.quote: To engage the safety mechanism, pull the safety mechanism fully to the rear towards the "S" position. See Picture 3.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 700, Seven, & 673 Bolt action centerfire rifles — Part No. 3509 rd Form RD 7055 rev. 0526 — Important Parts of the Firearm — The Safety Mechanism, p.7

steps.title: Magazine empty, bolt back, look and feel — twice
steps.action: If yours takes a detachable magazine, take it out; a floorplate rifle gets its plate opened and emptied. Raise the bolt handle, draw the bolt fully back, and look into the chamber and the magazine, then feel the chamber with a fingertip. Close under control and check a second time. Then look through the bore for any obstruction.
steps.quote: l. TO CHECK THE INSIDE OF THE BARREL: 1. Always point the firearm in a safe direction. 2. Place the safety mechanism in the "S" position. 3. Raise the bolt handle. 4. Pull the bolt all the way back. 5. Remove any ammunition from the chamber or magazine.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 700, Seven, & 673 Bolt action centerfire rifles — Part No. 3509 rd Form RD 7055 rev. 0526 — The Barrel — I. To check the inside of the barrel, p.9
steps.warn: NEVER try to remove an object from the barrel by loading another cartridge and firing.

steps.title: Bolt out at the release inside the trigger guard
steps.action: Bolt handle up, bolt fully back, then push the bolt stop release inside the front of the trigger guard and slide the bolt assembly out of the receiver. That is the pattern’s whole owner strip: the bolt stays in one piece, and the trigger assembly, stock screws and magazine system stay untouched — Ashbury Precision Ordnance’s work.
steps.quote: 4. Raise the bolt handle. 5. Pull the bolt handle all the way back. 6. Push the bolt stop release in the trigger guard. See Picture 8. 7. Slide the bolt assembly from the firearm.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 700, Seven, & 673 Bolt action centerfire rifles — Part No. 3509 rd Form RD 7055 rev. 0526 — To Remove The Bolt Assembly, steps 4-7, p.8

steps.title: Port down, and always from the chamber end
steps.action: Lay the rifle on its side with the ejection port facing down so solvent drains out instead of into the trigger. Clean the barrel from the chamber end to the muzzle: brush wet with solvent, dry patches until clean, a lightly oiled patch for storage, and a dry patch before the next shot. Wipe the bolt body and its lugs, and put a thin film of oil on the lugs and the bolt body where it rides.
steps.quote: NOTE: Barrel should lay horizontally with the ejection port facing down during cleaning. Always clean the barrel from the chamber end to the muzzle.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 700, Seven, & 673 Bolt action centerfire rifles — Part No. 3509 rd Form RD 7055 rev. 0526 — To Clean the Barrel — note between steps 4 and 5, p.13

steps.title: Look for the things that mean stop
steps.action: Hold the barrel up to the light and look through it: you want a clean, unbroken bore with no obstruction, no bulge and no dark ring. Look over the receiver, the barrel and the stock for cracks, the bolt’s locking lugs for chips, and for anything loose or missing. A screw or pin that has worked loose is reported, not tightened — how tight it should be is a question for Ashbury Precision Ordnance.
steps.prose: Any one of these means the gun is not fired until Ashbury Precision Ordnance has seen it.

deepAbsentReason: There is no deep clean for the Ashbury Precision Ordnance SABER-M700, and this guide will not invent one. No manual from Ashbury Precision Ordnance exists for this model; the pattern source documents a field strip and nothing deeper for an owner. Anything that needs more than this guide goes to Ashbury Precision Ordnance, not onto the bench.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Ejection port DOWN; always from the chamber end to the muzzle
Brush wet with bore solvent, then dry patches until clean
A lightly oiled patch for storage; a dry patch before the next shot

cleaning.name: BOLT & ACTION
tasks: Bolt body and lugs wiped, a thin film of oil on both
⛔ No solvent into the trigger assembly

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Wiped with a lightly oiled cloth
No solvent on wood, finishes or optics

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: Stored dry — never shut in a closed case while damp
Looked over for rust at every clean

reassembly.title: Lugs aligned, bolt home
reassembly.action: Align the lugs on the bolt assembly with the receiver’s cuts, slide the bolt fully in, and push the handle down to close.
reassembly.quote: 3. Align the lugs on the bolt assembly with the receiver. See Picture 8. 4.Slide the bolt assembly into the receiver and push all the way in.
reassembly.section: To Replace The Bolt Assembly, steps 3-4, p.9

reassembly.title: Check the barrel first
reassembly.action: Before the bolt went back you looked through the barrel — Remington prints that warning at exactly this point, and it is the one that catches a forgotten patch.
reassembly.quote: Before you replace the bolt assembly, make sure the barrel is free from obstructions.
reassembly.section: To Clean the Firearm, warning before step 5, p.13

fncheck: Chamber and magazine proven empty twice. Run Remington’s own test for this pattern: safety at F, close the bolt smartly — the firing pin must remain cocked — then pull the trigger; the firing pin must release. Remington’s instruction is to repeat that test at least ten times, and a firing pin that ever fails to stay cocked when the bolt closes means the rifle goes to Ashbury Precision Ordnance before it is loaded again. This dry test is the pattern source’s own, performed only on a rifle proven empty, muzzle at a safe backstop.
